body:
EPISODE PACKAGE
====

EPISODE TITLE: THE DAY WE GOT POETRY 8.2.1 APPRECIATION OF RIGHT
SUBJECT / TOPIC: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH / Poetry 8.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Stylistic devices in poetry: - Metonymy - Sy
GRADE: Grade 12
LENGTH TARGET: 5–10 minutes
LOGLINE: Learners nearly fail a real task linked to Poetry 8.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Stylistic devices in poetry: - Metonymy - Sy until they stop guessing and use the correct method.
SETTING: INT./EXT. Kenyan home, school, or market — present day

CAST
----
• NEEMA — curious learner who jumps to conclusions (school or home clothes)
• BARAKA — careful friend who checks evidence (everyday clothes)
• HALIMA — adult guide who asks for reasons, not slogans (apron / lab coat / lesso)

STORY GOAL
----
Complete a practical task correctly using Poetry 8.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Stylistic devices in poetry: - Metonymy - Sy

WRONG WAY VS RIGHT WAY
----
Wrong: Guessing or copying a rumour about Poetry 8.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Stylistic devices in poetry: - Metonymy - Sy
Right: Naming the idea correctly and applying a clear step-by-step check

SCENES
----

SCENE 1 — OPENING — DAY
NEEMA enters with a clear goal: Complete a practical task correctly using Poetry 8.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Stylistic devices in poetry: - Metonymy - Sy. Camera follows hands and faces.
NEEMA: "If I finish this today, I will finally understand it."
BARAKA: "Then stop guessing. Show me your first step."

SCENE 2 — OBSTACLE — DAY
A real-world obstacle appears. Props related to the topic are handled as real objects.
NEEMA: "It looks easy. Watch me do it the usual way."
HALIMA: "If you are wrong, we lose time — and maybe more."

SCENE 3 — WRONG WAY — DAY
WRONG WAY: Guessing or copying a rumour about Poetry 8.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Stylistic devices in poetry: - Metonymy - Sy. The problem worsens. Meaning stays in action — no reading notes aloud.
NEEMA: "See? That is what everyone says."
BARAKA: "And it got worse. Your idea is incomplete."

SCENE 4 — DISCOVERY — DAY
A clue appears through action — a label, a count, a safer method, a remembered rule spoken while doing.
BARAKA: "Look at what actually changed. Name it properly."
NEEMA: "Wait… if that is true, I was checking the wrong thing."

SCENE 5 — RIGHT WAY — DAY
RIGHT WAY: Naming the idea correctly and applying a clear step-by-step check. Characters perform the corrected action step by step.
NEEMA: "This time we follow the rule, not the rumour."
HALIMA: "I can see the difference already."

SCENE 6 — SECOND TEST — DAY
A new obstacle forces them to apply the idea again, proving it was not luck.
HALIMA: "We are not done. Another problem just arrived."
BARAKA: "Same idea. Fresh situation. Go."

SCENE 7 — RESOLUTION — DAY
Payoff: goal achieved. Characters show the result without a lecture voice-over.
NEEMA: "It worked because we used the idea correctly."
BARAKA: "Say the reason in your own words before we pack up."

SCENE 8 — BUTTON — DAY
Final acted beat tying emotion to learning.
HALIMA: "Next time someone guesses, we will ask for the reason."
NEEMA: "And we will check the evidence first."

REFLECTION BEAT (ON SCREEN, ACTED)
----
BARAKA: "What evidence shows you understood Poetry 8.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Stylistic devices in poetry: - Metonymy - Sy?"
NEEMA: "A correct definition + one local example + one corrected mistake"

Study pages covered: 20 pages on Poetry 8.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry Stylistic devices in poetry: - Metonymy - Sy.
